entries.subject: DAMIT 16284: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-16284.txt. Model 16284, version 2023-10-03, pole (264°, -2°), period 14.93046 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 103 ±7 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2023), Scaling slowly rotating asteroids with stellar occultations
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2023), Scaling slowly rotating asteroids with stellar occultations](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...679A..60M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 118.86 ± 1.76 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 275 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 16283, pole ['85', '-10'], [Model 16283](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/16283) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 16283: pole (85°, -10°), 14.93045 h, version 2023-10-03, archive diameter 98 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "51.5 km (size-calibrated model)" (damit-models) implies a diameter of 103 km, outside the added NEOWISE V2.0 neowise_mainbelt.csv record 225 (Masiero et al. 2014) diameter 95.475 ± 1.112 km (NEOWISE, NEATM). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.

entries.subject: Sapientia whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 20 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.927 at 462 nm, 1.019 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#403e3b in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 4.9% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.9%), from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2012, ApJ 759, L8; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
